parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no facility or custody bans, no documented police targeting of trans visitors, and the violent record is dated (2012–2013) with no recent incidents documented; functioning institutions, a visible trans community and rising acceptance (70% in 2024) support a reduced-risk profile. The main current traveller-facing exposure is the wartime border practice: holders of male markers are stopped at the border and trans people need NGO help to reissue documents — a real, current universal friction, though not punitive, and it bites exit/entry processing more than street life. Hate-crime aggravation excludes gender identity and police response to violence was historically weak (dated), and open questions remain (custody placement, whether rule-of-law roadmap protections took effect). Acceptance-without-full-protection tier: 0.65.
